_Decidingandchoosing


                    Decisions   and  judgements
                    Note the collocations in bold in these emails between colleagues.
                                        in     in     amaile


                     eee                                       =]                             Reply

                      Hi Rita,
                      Have you made a decision yet about the new job? It must be difficult. It’s such a big decision to
                      have to move to London and everything. | always put off making decisions till the last possible
                      moment.  | bet you’re the same. | detected a slight hesitation in your last email. Are you having
                      second thoughts? Anyway, let me know.
                      Paul

                     eee                                                                      Reply
                      Dear Carl,
                      You’ve probably heard that the management have taken the decision to close the Madrid office.
                      There was a lot of discussion, but apparently it was a unanimous decision in the end. There’s
                      always been a degree of uncertainty surrounding the future of the Madrid office, but let’s just
                      hope this will now be seen as a wise decision by everyone.
                      Elizabeth

                                                                                               Reply

                      Dear Mary,
                      After weeks of hesitating, it seems Matt has arrived at a decision about the research fund. He’s
                      going to increase it by £10,000. | think that’s a sensible decision that combines generosity and
                      sound judgement.  But he’s also defending his decision to close down the San Antonio project,
                      which is losing a lot of money. However, he’s reserving judgement on the Berlin project until he
                      gets more reliable information.
                      Nick


                    Choices,   opportunities,    advice                                                  |
                     Tim:   I’m going to have to make A choice soon about next year. I’ve been 4 4
                            given the chance of going on A six-month expedition to South           |
                            America and I’ve been offered A job in A bookshop here.                             A
                    Laura:  Wow! South America! That sounds like the opportunity
                            of A lifetime! How could you say no?
                     Tim:   Well, believe it or not, | don’t have A burning desire to
                            see the world, I’d much prefer just to stay at home. Anyway, I’m \      ||   |
                            going to consider all the options before | decide.
                    Laura:  Well, | know you never take my advice but | would strongly advise ~~
                            you to think of the future. Overseas experience is much more useful than working in your home
                            town. You’re lucky to have A choice, A lot of people stay at home because they have no option.
                      Tim:  | know, | know, but it’s a tough choice. You wouldn’t understand.
                    Laura:  Well, | think you’re just taking the soft option if you choose the bookshop. | can’t believe
                            you’re going to pass up the opportunity of a trip to South America.
                      Tim:  Well, we all face difficult choices now and then.
                    Laura:  Difficult! You’re mad! Look, just don’t reject South America out of hand. Promise me
                            think about it.
                      Tim:  Yes, yes, | already said I’m going to weigh up the options and come to a decision.
